definition_en: a violent collision or its sound, or to hit something hard and break
core_image: 两辆车头撞在一起，玻璃碎成一地亮点
scene: 清晨的十字路口，两辆车头撞在一起，玻璃撒了一地。The two cars crashed at the crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 crash 指「碰撞」（第 1 个义项：车辆猛烈相撞）；句意是两辆车在路口撞上了。

senses.title: Two things hitting hard
senses.definition: a violent collision between vehicles or objects
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或物体之间的猛烈相撞
senses.example: The crash blocked the whole road.
senses.exampleCN: 这场碰撞把整条路都堵住了。
senses.why: Two paths meet and both refuse to bend.
senses.whyCN: 两条路线相遇，两边都不肯让。

senses.title: An aircraft coming down
senses.definition: the falling and breaking of an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 飞行器坠落并损毁
senses.example: The plane crash was a terrible accident.
senses.exampleCN: 那场空难是一场可怕的意外。
senses.why: What flies must also obey the ground.
senses.whyCN: 会飞的东西，也终究要听地面的话。

senses.title: A market falling down
senses.definition: a sudden failure of a market or a system
senses.definitionCN: 市场或系统的突然失效
senses.example: The market crash ruined many families.
senses.exampleCN: 市场崩溃让许多家庭破了产。
senses.why: Numbers can fall as fast as metal can.
senses.whyCN: 数字下坠的速度，不比金属慢。

intro.en: Crash comes from Middle English crasschen, to make a loud clattering noise, a word built from its own sound.
intro.cn: crash 源自中古英语 crasschen（发出噼啪巨响），是照着声音造出来的词。

items.en: Crasschen meant to make a loud clattering noise.
items.cn: crasschen 意为发出响亮的碰撞声。

items.en: Crash named the sound of something breaking.
items.cn: crash 指东西碎裂时的响声。

items.en: It came to name a violent collision itself.
items.cn: 它转而来指猛烈碰撞这件事本身。

items.en: Crash widened to aircraft and to money markets.
items.cn: crash 又扩展到飞机与金融市场。

items.en: It now covers traffic, planes, computers and prices.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖交通、飞机、电脑与价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin with a hard cr-, and the meaning group names other words for violent impact.
note.cn: 形近组收集以硬辅音 cr- 开头的词，近义组列出其他表示猛烈撞击的说法。

entries.definition: to press something until it breaks
a sharp disagreement or fight
a hard outer layer
the hitting together of two moving things
to break loudly into pieces
a badly damaged ship or vehicle

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two bumpers meeting, then move to a falling plane and to a falling market.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个保险杠相碰开始，再到坠落的飞机，最后到崩落的市场。

normal.en: Crash sounds like what it means: a hard thing meeting a hard thing.
normal.cn: crash 读起来就像它的意思：硬东西撞上硬东西。

normal.en: Glass tells the story best, because it breaks all at once.
normal.cn: 玻璃最能说明问题，因为它是整片一起碎的。

normal.en: A crash course is a short road driven at full speed.
normal.cn: 速成课就是全速开完的一小段路。

normal.en: A plane crash ends in silence after the noise.
normal.cn: 空难总是在巨响之后归于寂静。

normal.en: Prices crash the way glass does: no warning, then nothing.
normal.cn: 价格崩落像玻璃：没有预告，然后什么都没有。

abstract.en: Picture two metal heads touching at speed.
abstract.cn: 想象两个金属车头高速相触。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart dropping straight down.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线笔直落下。

abstract.en: Picture a shower of small bright pieces on the road.
abstract.cn: 想象路面上撒开一片明亮的小碎片。

examples.en: The truck crashed into the fence.
examples.cn: 卡车撞上了篱笆。

examples.en: He survived a plane crash last winter.
examples.cn: 他去年冬天经历了一场空难并活了下来。

examples.en: The stock market crashed in a single day.
examples.cn: 股市在一天之内崩盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crash 记成「咔嚓」加 sh：撞上去那一声碎响，就是 crash。

root: 源自中古英语 crasschen（发出噼啪巨响），是拟声词，本指物体碎裂的响声，后指猛烈碰撞，近代又扩展到飞机坠毁与市场崩溃。

sensesIntro.en: From two cars meeting to a plane coming down and a market losing its floor.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两车相撞，到飞机坠落，最后到市场失去支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hard fronts meeting with a burst of glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个坚硬的车头相撞，玻璃四溅。

branches.en: Two moving things reach the same point at once.
branches.cn: 两个运动的东西同时到达同一点。

branches.en: What flies can lose the air under it.
branches.cn: 会飞的东西也会失去身下的空气。

branches.en: A system built on numbers can fall like metal.
branches.cn: 建立在数字上的系统也能像金属一样跌落。

branches.en: Both end with broken parts on the ground.
branches.cn: 两者都以碎片落地收场。

branches.en: The same word covers a lost plane and a lost fortune.
branches.cn: 同一个词既说失事的飞机，也说失去的财富。

intro.en: Crash is an imitative base word that builds compounds with course, landing and proof.
intro.cn: crash 是拟声词根，可与 course、landing、proof 等组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English; Latin offers no source for this crash.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，拉丁语并不能给它提供来源。

items.example: The waves crashed on the rocks.
A crashing sound came from the hall.
A party crasher ate all the cake.
items.exampleCN: 一个闯入者吃光了蛋糕。

items.meaning: a short fast course of study
items.example: He took a crash course in Spanish.
items.exampleCN: 他上了一门西班牙语速成课。

items.meaning: a landing that damages the aircraft
items.example: The pilot made a crash landing.

definition_en: mad or unable to think normally, extremely fond of something, or very foolish
core_image: 一个人把椅子顶在头上，在雨里转圈大笑
scene: 他把椅子顶在头上，在雨里转着圈大笑。The neighbours thought he was crazy.
sceneCN: 这里 crazy 指「疯狂的」（第 1 个义项：精神或行为失去常态）；句意是邻居们都觉得他疯了。

senses.title: A mind out of order
senses.definition: mad, or unable to think or behave in a normal way
senses.definitionCN: 精神失常，或无法正常思考和行事
senses.example: The noise nearly drove him crazy.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪声几乎把他逼疯。
senses.why: When the mind loses its order, the body does strange things.
senses.whyCN: 脑子一乱，身体就做出古怪的举动。

senses.title: Wildly fond of something
senses.definition: extremely fond of something or someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某物或某人喜欢到极点
senses.example: She is crazy about old films.
senses.exampleCN: 她对老电影着迷得不得了。
senses.why: Love also takes away the usual measure.
senses.whyCN: 喜欢到极点，也会拿走平常的分寸。

senses.title: A plan without sense
senses.definition: very foolish or unreasonable
senses.definitionCN: 极为愚蠢或不合理的
senses.example: It is a crazy plan that cannot work.
senses.exampleCN: 这是个不可能成功的荒唐计划。
senses.why: A plan without measure looks like a mind without order.
senses.whyCN: 没有分寸的计划，就像没有秩序的脑子。

intro.en: Crazy grows from Middle English crasen, to shatter, so it first meant full of cracks and unsound.
intro.cn: crazy 由中古英语 crasen（碎裂）而来，所以最初意为「满是裂缝、不结实」。

items.en: Crasen meant to break or shatter.
items.cn: crasen 意为打碎或裂开。

items.en: Crazy first meant full of cracks and unsound.
items.cn: crazy 最初指布满裂缝、不牢靠。

items.en: It came to mean a mind that is cracked.
items.cn: 它转而指「裂了缝的脑子」。

items.en: It widened to mean wildly fond of something.
items.cn: 它又扩展为对某物喜欢到发狂。

items.en: It now covers madness, passion and foolish plans.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖发疯、痴迷与荒唐的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near crazy in shape, and the meaning group names other words for foolish or wild.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 crazy 的词，近义组列出其他表示疯狂与愚蠢的说法。

entries.definition: a fashion that everyone follows for a while
driven mad by strong feeling
entries.definitionCN: 被强烈情绪逼得失常的

entries.definition: a line pressed into cloth or paper
entries.definitionCN: 布料或纸上压出的折痕

entries.definition: mentally ill or wildly foolish
entries.definitionCN: 精神失常或荒唐至极的

entries.definition: lacking good sense
out of control and full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 失去控制且充满蛮劲的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with cracks in a pot, then move to a cracked mind and to a passion with no measure.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从罐子上的裂缝开始，再到裂了缝的脑子，最后到没有分寸的痴迷。

normal.en: Crazy comes from a word for cracked, and a cracked pot cannot hold water.
normal.cn: crazy 来自「裂」这个词，裂了的罐子存不住水。

normal.en: A cracked mind lets strange ideas leak out.
normal.cn: 脑子裂了缝，古怪的念头就漏出来。

normal.en: Being crazy about a film is a happy crack in the heart.
normal.cn: 对一部电影着迷，是心里一条快乐的裂缝。

normal.en: A crazy plan is a bridge with no supports.
normal.cn: 荒唐的计划，是一座没有支柱的桥。

normal.en: Noise repeated all day can crack anyone's calm.
normal.cn: 噪声一整天不停，能敲裂任何人的平静。

abstract.en: Picture a hairline crack running down a clay pot.
abstract.cn: 想象一道发丝般的裂缝从陶罐上延伸下来。

abstract.en: Picture a man laughing in the rain with a chair on his head.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头顶椅子在雨里大笑的人。

abstract.en: Picture a map with the roads drawn in the wrong places.
abstract.cn: 想象一张把路画错位置的地图。

examples.en: He is crazy about fast cars.
examples.cn: 他对快车着迷。

examples.en: It was a crazy idea, but it worked.
examples.cn: 那是个疯狂的想法，但它奏效了。

examples.en: The children drove their mother crazy with noise.
examples.cn: 孩子们吵得妈妈要发疯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crazy 记成 crack（裂）加 y：脑子裂了缝，人就成了 crazy。

root: 源自中古英语 crasen（碎裂）；crazy 本指「满是裂缝、不结实的」，后指「脑子出了裂缝」即发疯，再引申为极度着迷与荒唐。

sensesIntro.en: From a cracked thing, to a mind that loses order, to a fondness that has no limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从裂了的东西，到失去秩序的脑子，最后到没有限度的喜欢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack opening in something that should be whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该完整的东西上裂开一道缝。

branches.en: A mind with a crack no longer follows one line.
branches.cn: 裂了缝的脑子不再沿着一条线走。

branches.en: Passion also breaks the usual limits of attention.
branches.cn: 痴迷同样打破了注意力的常规限度。

branches.en: A plan with no support looks like a cracked wall.
branches.cn: 没有支撑的计划，像一堵裂开的墙。

branches.en: Both are states where measure has been lost.
branches.cn: 两者都是失去分寸的状态。

branches.en: Love and folly both ignore what others call sense.
branches.cn: 痴迷与荒唐，都不理别人所谓的分寸。

intro.en: Crazy begins with the base craze and takes the endings -y, -ily and -iness.
intro.cn: crazy 以词基 craze 为底，加上 -y、-ily 与 -iness 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; Latin has no share in this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语，拉丁语与它无关。

items.meaningCN: 满是裂缝的，继而指发疯
items.exampleCN: 这个计划听起来很疯狂。

items.example: Each idea was crazier than the last.
items.exampleCN: 每个主意都比上一个更荒唐。

items.example: That was the craziest week of my life.
items.exampleCN: 那是我一生中最疯狂的一周。

items.example: He drove crazily down the hill.

items.exampleCN: 到早晨，那股疯狂劲就过去了。
这种玩具成了一阵风潮。

items.example: A crazed look crossed his face.

items.meaningCN: 被关久了而烦躁不安的
items.example: The crew grew stir-crazy below deck.
items.exampleCN: 船员在甲板下憋得烦躁起来。

definition_en: to make something new that did not exist before
core_image: 一张白纸上第一次画出一扇门，推开就是新房间
scene: 白纸上本来什么都没有，她一笔画出第一扇门。The writer created a whole world in three pages.
sceneCN: 这里 create 指「创造」（第 1 个义项：从无到有地做出新东西）；句意是作者用三页纸创造了一整个世界。

senses.title: To make something new
senses.definition: to make something new that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 做出以前不存在的全新事物
senses.example: They created a garden on the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋顶上造了一个花园。
senses.why: A blank space waits for the first line.
senses.whyCN: 一片空白总在等第一笔。

senses.title: To make a work of art
senses.definition: to produce a work of art or writing
senses.definitionCN: 产出艺术作品或文字作品
senses.example: She created a character we all remember.
senses.exampleCN: 她创作了一个我们都记得的角色。
senses.why: A story begins as nothing and then has a face.
senses.whyCN: 故事从无开始，然后长出一张脸。

senses.title: To cause a situation
senses.definition: to cause a situation or a problem to happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状况或问题发生
senses.example: The new road created a lot of noise.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的路带来了很多噪声。
senses.why: Every new thing pushes the old arrangement aside.
senses.whyCN: 每件新东西都会把旧的安排挤到一边。

intro.en: Create comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, a word related to crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: create 源自拉丁语 creare（制造、使生成），与 crescere（生长）同源。

items.en: Creare meant to make, bring forth or appoint.
items.cn: creare 意为制造、使产生或任命。

items.en: Crescere, to grow, shared the same old root.
items.cn: 表示生长的 crescere 与它共用一个古老词根。

items.en: Creatio named the act of making.
items.cn: creatio 指制造这一行为。

items.en: Create entered English as a word for divine making.
items.cn: create 进入英语时，多指神明造物。

items.en: It now covers art, jobs, problems and accounts.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖艺术创作、就业、问题与账户。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near create in shape, and the meaning group names other words for bringing something into being.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 create 的词，近义组列出其他表示「使某物出现」的说法。

entries.definition: a living animal or being
to burn a body to ashes
a large box for carrying goods
to form something from parts
to think of and build something new
to bring something into existence

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with an empty page, then move to a story and to a change nobody asked for.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张空页开始，再到一个故事，最后到一场没人要求的变化。

normal.en: Create and grow share a root: to create is to let something grow out of nothing.
normal.cn: create 与「生长」同根：创造就是让东西从无里长出来。

normal.en: The first line on a blank page is always the bravest.
normal.cn: 白纸上的第一笔，总是最勇敢的一笔。

normal.en: A writer creates people who never breathe but stay alive.
normal.cn: 作家创造的人从不呼吸，却一直活着。

normal.en: A new road creates noise as well as shortcuts.
normal.cn: 新路带来捷径，也带来噪声。

normal.en: To create an account is to open a small new room.
normal.cn: 创建一个账户，就是开出一间小小的新房间。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil touching white paper for the first time.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔第一次碰到白纸。

abstract.en: Picture a door drawn on a wall, opening inward.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上画着一扇朝里开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a small seed pushing soil upward.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒小种子把泥土顶起来。

examples.en: The company plans to create two hundred jobs.
examples.cn: 这家公司计划创造两百个就业岗位。

examples.en: He created the whole design on a single sheet.
examples.cn: 他在一张纸上完成了整个设计。

examples.en: Loud music can create tension between neighbours.
examples.cn: 大声的音乐会在邻里之间造成紧张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 create 记成 cre（生长）加 ate：让原本没有的东西长出来，就是创造。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（制造、使生成、任命），与 crescere（生长）同源，本指使某物生成，后指从无到有地造出，也指引起某种状况。

sensesIntro.en: From a blank page to a made world and to the changes that follow it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张白纸，到被造出的世界，最后到随之而来的种种变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first line appearing on empty paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：空白的纸上出现第一笔。

branches.en: Something new is drawn where nothing stood.
branches.cn: 在原本空无的地方画出了新东西。

branches.en: A made character can outlive the hand that drew it.
branches.cn: 被创作的角色能比画它的手活得更久。

branches.en: Every new thing also makes old things move.
branches.cn: 每件新东西也会叫旧东西让位。

branches.en: To create a thing and to create a story share one gesture.
branches.cn: 造物与创作，共用同一个动作。

branches.en: Works and problems both begin with someone acting.
branches.cn: 作品与麻烦，都始于有人动手。

intro.en: Create grows from the Latin making base cre-, with forms in -es, -ed, -ing and nouns in -ion and -or.
intro.cn: create 从拉丁语表示制造的词基 cre- 长出，带 -es、-ed、-ing 等变形，及 -ion、-or 等名词。

latinIntro.en: The making base creare also shapes creation, creator and creature.
latinIntro.cn: 表示制造的词基 creare 也构成 creation、creator 与 creature。

items.meaning: to bring something new into being

items.exampleCN: 这座公园建于一九零零年。

items.example: She is creating a new pattern.
items.exampleCN: 她正在创造一种新花样。

items.meaning: the act or result of making
the power to make new things

definition_zh: 创造；创建；创作；创作物；产物
definition_en: the act of making something exist that did not exist before, or the thing that is made
core_image: 空白的画布上落下第一笔，一件原本不存在的东西出现了
scene: 美术馆的展厅里，人们围在一幅巨大的新画前低声赞叹，作者站在角落。Everyone admired the young artist's latest creation.
sceneCN: 这里 creation 指「创作物」（第 3 个义项：被创作出来的具体作品）；句意是所有人都赞叹这位年轻画家最新的作品。

senses.title: The act of making something new
senses.definition: the act or process of making something exist that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 使原本不存在的东西得以存在的行为或过程
senses.example: The creation of new jobs helped the town recover.
senses.exampleCN: 新岗位的创造帮助这个镇子恢复了元气。
senses.why: The Latin stem creare means to bring forth, so the noun first names the act of bringing forth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 creare 意为「使生出」，所以名词首先指「使生出」这一行为本身。

senses.title: The act of inventing or designing
senses.definition: the act of producing a work of art, writing, or design using imagination
senses.definitionCN: 凭想象力产出艺术、文字或设计作品的行为
senses.example: The creation of the character took the author ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个人物的创作花了作者十年时间。
senses.why: When what is brought forth is imagined rather than manufactured, the word narrows to artistic making.
senses.whyCN: 当「生出」的东西来自想象而非制造时，这个词收窄为艺术创作。

senses.title: A thing that has been made
senses.definition: something that someone has made or invented, especially something unusual or imaginative
senses.definitionCN: 某人造出或发明的东西，尤指独特或富有想象力之物
senses.example: The garden is his most unusual creation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园是他最不寻常的创作。
senses.why: A finished act of making leaves behind an object, so the noun also names the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 完成的创造会留下一个对象，于是名词也转指这个被造出来的东西。

senses.title: The making of the world
senses.definition: the making of the world and everything in it, especially in religious belief
senses.definitionCN: 世界及其中万物的被造，尤见于宗教信仰
senses.example: The story describes the creation of the world in seven days.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事讲述了世界在七日内被造的过程。
senses.why: Only a supreme maker can bring the whole world forth, so the word rises to the cosmic scale.
senses.whyCN: 能把整个世界生出来的唯有至高造物者，于是这个词升格到宇宙尺度。

senses.title: The whole world of living things
senses.definition: all the living things in the world, thought of together
senses.definitionCN: 把世上一切生灵合起来看的整体
senses.example: All creation seemed to fall silent before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，天地众生仿佛都安静了下来。
senses.why: Every living thing is a made thing, so the made world as a whole can be called creation.
senses.whyCN: 每个生灵都是被造之物，于是被造的世界整体也可以称为「万物」。

intro.en: Creation comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, through creatio, the act of making.
intro.cn: creation 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），经 creatio（创造行为）进入英语。

items.en: The root *ker- is generally reconstructed as meaning to grow or make grow.
items.cn: 词根 *ker- 一般被重构为「生长、使生长」之义。

items.en: Creare meant to make something come forth or grow; creatio named the act of making.
items.cn: creare 意为使某物生出或生长；creatio 指创造这一行为。

items.en: Creacion carried the same religious and general sense of making.
items.cn: creacion 带有同样泛指与宗教意义上的「创造」义。

items.en: Creation first appeared in English chiefly for the making of the world by God.
items.cn: creation 初入英语时主要指上天创造世界。

items.en: It widened to any act of making and to the thing made, including works of art.
items.cn: 它扩展为任何创造行为及其产物，包括艺术作品。

items.en: It now covers founding things, inventing designs, and naming the results.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖创建事物、设计发明，并指创造出来的成果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the creat- stem, and the near-meaning group names other acts or results of making.
note.cn: 形近组共享 creat- 词干，近义组列出其他表示创造行为或成果的说法。

entries.definition: to make something new exist
good at making new and original things
entries.definitionCN: 善于造出新颖原创之物的

entries.definition: a person or force that makes something
a new device or idea that someone has thought up
entries.definitionCN: 想出来的新装置或新点子

entries.definition: a piece of art, music, or writing
entries.definitionCN: 一件艺术、音乐或文字作品

entries.definition: a work of art made with great skill
entries.definitionCN: 以高超技艺完成的艺术作品

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the first stroke on a blank canvas to the finished thing hanging on the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从空白画布上的第一笔，一直走到挂在墙上的成品。

normal.en: Create plus -ion: the act of creating, then the thing created.
normal.cn: create 加 -ion：先指创造这一行为，再指被造出来的东西。

normal.en: Creation = creation of jobs, creation of art, creation of the world.
normal.cn: creation 的三大常用面：创造岗位、艺术创作、创世。

normal.en: Every creation needs a creator.
normal.cn: 每件创作物背后都有一个创造者。

normal.en: The -ion ending turns the verb into a noun you can count.
normal.cn: -ion 后缀把动词变成可数的名词。

normal.en: Creation and creative share the same first letters and the same family.
normal.cn: creation 与 creative 同头同族，一起记。

abstract.en: Picture the first brushstroke on a blank canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象空白画布上落下的第一笔。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay slowly becoming a figure.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土慢慢变成一个人像。

abstract.en: Picture a newborn star lighting an empty sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗新星照亮空无一物的天空。

examples.en: The creation of the park took only two years.
examples.cn: 这座公园的建成只花了两年。

examples.en: Her latest creation won first prize at the fair.
examples.cn: 她的最新作品在展会上得了头奖。

examples.en: They discussed stories about the creation of the world.
examples.cn: 他们讨论了关于创世的种种故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creation 记成 create（创造）加 -ion：创造这一行为是创造，创造出来的东西也是创作，一横一竖正好两个方向。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），名词形式 creatio 指「创造行为」，经古法语 creacion 于十四世纪进入英语；本义是「使某物生出」，先专指上天创世，后扩展到一切创造行为及其产物。

sensesIntro.en: From the bare act of making something exist, creation widens to artistic invention, then to the thing made, and finally to the making of the world itself.
sensesIntro.cn: creation 从「使某物存在」的赤裸行为出发，扩展到艺术创作，再转指创作物，最终上升到创世与天地众生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first stroke on a blank canvas — something now exists that did not exist before
core.cn: 核心意象：空白画布上的第一笔——原本不存在的东西从此存在了

branches.en: Bringing jobs, systems, or organizations into existence.
branches.cn: 使岗位、体系或组织从无到有。

branches.en: Imagining and designing a work of art or writing.
branches.cn: 凭想象设计与产出艺术或文字作品。

branches.en: The finished object that the act of making leaves behind.
branches.cn: 创造行为留下的成品本身。

branches.en: The religious account of the world being made.
branches.cn: 宗教中世界被造的叙事。

branches.en: All living things viewed as one made world.
branches.cn: 把一切生灵看作同一个被造的世界。

intro.en: Creation is built from a Latin verb stem plus a noun suffix; the same family shares one stem.
intro.cn: creation 由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀构成；同族词共享同一个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Latin creare, and the suffix -ion goes back to Latin -io, which turns verbs into nouns of action.
latinIntro.cn: 词干可追溯到拉丁语 creare，后缀 -ion 源自拉丁语 -io，用于把动词变成表行为的名词。

items.example: create means to make something new
items.exampleCN: create 意为造出新的东西

items.example: action means the act of doing
items.exampleCN: action 意为做这件事的行为

items.example: creativity means the quality of being creative

definition_zh: 有创造力的；创作性的；创意人员
definition_en: good at making new things or ideas, or relating to such making
core_image: 桌上散着纸片和线头，中间立着一个刚拧成的小装置
scene: 桌上散着纸片和线头，他随手把它们拧成一个奇怪的小装置。She found a creative solution to the noise problem.
sceneCN: 这里 creative 指「有创造力的」（第 1 个义项：善于想出并做出新东西）；句意是她为噪声问题想出了一个有创意的办法。

senses.title: Full of new ideas
senses.definition: able to think of new and original ideas
senses.definitionCN: 能想出新颖独到的点子
senses.example: She is the most creative person in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她是班上最有创造力的人。
senses.why: The mind refuses the first easy answer.
senses.whyCN: 这样的脑子不肯接受第一个省事的答案。

senses.title: Involving imagination
senses.definition: involving imagination in making something
senses.definitionCN: 在制作过程中需要想象力的
senses.example: He teaches creative writing at school.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校教创意写作。
senses.why: Some work begins with a blank page, not a rule.
senses.whyCN: 有些工作从一张白纸开始，而不是从一条规则开始。

senses.title: A person paid for ideas
senses.definition: a person whose job is to produce ideas
senses.definitionCN: 以想出点子为职业的人
senses.example: The agency hired two creatives.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司聘了两名创意人员。
senses.why: Every industry needs someone to imagine first.
senses.whyCN: 每个行业都需要有人先想一步。

intro.en: Creative joins Latin creare, to make, with the adjective ending -ive.
intro.cn: creative 由拉丁语 creare（制造）与形容词词尾 -ive 构成。

items.en: Creare meant to make or bring forth.
items.cn: creare 意为制造或使产生。

items.en: Creativus named the power to make.
items.cn: creativus 指制造的能力。

items.en: Creative described the power of a maker.
items.cn: creative 形容创造者的能力。

items.en: It widened to art and to original thought.
items.cn: 它扩展到艺术与独到的想法。

items.en: It now also names people paid for their ideas.
items.cn: 今天它也可以指靠点子吃饭的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the create base or a similar ending, and the meaning group names other words for original thinking.
note.cn: 形近组共享 create 词基或相近词尾，近义组列出其他表示原创想法的说法。

entries.definition: a person who makes something new
the act or result of making
acting only after something happens
entries.definitionCN: 只在事情发生后才作出反应的

entries.definition: new and not copied from others
full of pictures in the mind
good at thinking up new things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pile of odd pieces, then move to a blank page and to a paid idea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一堆零碎东西开始，再到一张白纸，最后到一份能卖钱的点。

normal.en: Creative is create with -ive: the quality of being able to make.
normal.cn: creative 就是 create 加 -ive：能造出东西的那种性质。

normal.en: A creative person keeps the odd pieces others throw away.
normal.cn: 有创造力的人会留下别人扔掉的零碎。

normal.en: Two sticks and a string can become a small machine.
normal.cn: 两根棍一段线，也能变成一台小机器。

normal.en: Creative writing starts where the rule book stops.
normal.cn: 创意写作从规则手册结束的地方开始。

normal.en: An agency pays creatives for the ideas it cannot order.
normal.cn: 公司花钱请创意人员，因为他们买不来被命令出的点子。

abstract.en: Picture a table covered with paper, wire and tape.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摆满纸片、铁丝和胶带的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing that follows no straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅没有一条直线的画。

abstract.en: Picture a light bulb drawn where a full stop should be.
abstract.cn: 想象本该是句号的地方画了一只灯泡。

examples.en: She is creative with very little money.
examples.cn: 她用很少的钱也能做出新花样。

examples.en: The school runs a creative writing club.
examples.cn: 学校办了一个创意写作社。

examples.en: The firm hires young creatives every spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司每年春天都招年轻创意人员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creative 记成 create（创造）加 ive（有…性质的）：有创造性质的，就是有创造力。

root: 由拉丁语 creare（制造、生成）加形容词词尾 -ive 构成；creare 与 crescere（生长）同源，本指「具有生成能力的」，后专指富有创造力与原创想法。

sensesIntro.en: From a mind that refuses the easy answer, to work that begins with a blank page, to people paid for ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 从不肯接受省事答案的脑子，到从白纸开始的工作，最后到靠点子吃饭的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: odd pieces joined into a shape nobody planned.
core.cn: 核心意象：零碎的东西被拼成没人计划过的形状。

branches.en: The mind keeps looking after the first answer fails.
branches.cn: 第一个答案不行之后，脑子还在继续找。

branches.en: Some work asks for imagination instead of rules.
branches.cn: 有些工作要求想象，而不是规则。

branches.en: An industry pays for the first picture in someone's head.
branches.cn: 行业愿意为某人脑中的第一幅图付钱。

branches.en: The person and the work share one quality of making.
branches.cn: 人与作品共享同一种「造」的品质。

branches.en: A creative job turns ideas into things others can use.
branches.cn: 创意工作把点子变成别人能用的东西。

intro.en: Creative is create plus the adjective ending -ive, and it grows its own nouns and adverbs.
intro.cn: creative 是 create 加形容词词尾 -ive，自身又能长出名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin making base creare lies under creative, creation and creator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示制造的词基 creare 垫在 creative、creation 与 creator 之下。

items.example: He created the logo last year.
items.exampleCN: 他去年设计了这个标志。

items.example: They are creating a new app.
items.exampleCN: 他们正在做一个新应用。

items.meaning: the act or result of making
the power to make new things

definition_zh: 生物；动物；人（带怜爱或轻蔑语气）
definition_en: a living animal or person, especially one shaped by nature
core_image: 草丛里一双发亮的眼睛盯着你，看不出那是什么
scene: 夜里草丛忽然一动，一双眼睛反着月光。Something small and alive was moving in the grass, a creature we could not name.
sceneCN: 这里 creature 指「生物」（第 1 个义项：有生命的动物或人）；句意是草丛里有种小小的活物在动，一种我们叫不出名字的生物。

senses.title: A living being
senses.definition: a living animal or person
senses.definitionCN: 有生命的动物或人
senses.example: Every creature needs water and air.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个生物都需要水和空气。
senses.why: Life is what all breathing things share.
senses.whyCN: 凡是会呼吸的东西，都共享生命。

senses.title: An animal
senses.definition: an animal, especially a small or unfamiliar one
senses.definitionCN: 动物，尤指微小或不熟悉的动物
senses.example: The pond is full of tiny creatures.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里满是微小的生物。
senses.why: A word is needed for animals too small to name.
senses.whyCN: 总得有个词来称呼小到叫不出名字的动物。

senses.title: A person, with pity
senses.definition: a person, spoken of with pity or contempt
senses.definitionCN: 带着怜悯或轻蔑去说一个人
senses.example: The poor creature had nowhere to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 这个可怜的人无处可睡。
senses.why: People are living things too, so the word can carry pity.
senses.whyCN: 人也是活物，所以这个词能带上怜悯。

intro.en: Creature comes from Latin creare, to make or bring forth, through creatura, a thing made.
intro.cn: creature 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生出），经 creatura（被造之物）进入英语。

items.en: Creare meant to make something grow or come forth.
items.cn: creare 意为使某物生长或出现。

items.en: Creatura named anything that had been brought into being.
items.cn: creatura 指一切被带进存在之中的东西。

items.en: Creature named a created living thing.
items.cn: creature 指被创造的活物。

items.en: Creature first meant any being made by God.
items.cn: creature 最初指上天所造的任何存在。

items.en: It now usually means an animal, or a person seen with pity.
items.cn: 今天它通常指动物，或带着怜悯去看的一个人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the creat- stem, and the meaning group names other living things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 creat- 这个词干，近义组列出其他表示生命体的说法。

entries.definition: to make something new
the act of making something
a person who makes something
a living thing that is not a plant
anything that is alive
a single living body

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a shape in the grass and end with a face you almost know.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从草丛里的一个影子开始，最后落到一张你几乎认得的脸。

normal.en: Create plus -ure: something created and left alive.
normal.cn: create 加 -ure：被造出来又活着的东西。

normal.en: Four legs, two eyes, one warm body.
normal.cn: 四条腿，两只眼，一具温热的身体。

normal.en: If it moves by itself, it is a creature.
normal.cn: 能自己动的东西，就是生物。

normal.en: A creature keeps no diary; it just keeps breathing.
normal.cn: 生物不写日记，它只管呼吸。

normal.en: Call it a creature when you cannot name the animal.
normal.cn: 叫不出名字时，就称它一声生物。

abstract.en: Picture eyes shining in a dark hedge.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗树篱里发亮的眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a shell moving slowly across wet sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只壳在湿沙上缓缓移动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that is not quite human.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不太像人的手。

examples.en: A small creature ran across the path.
examples.cn: 一只小生物跑过小路。

examples.en: The cave is home to creatures that avoid light.
examples.cn: 这洞穴是避光生物的家。

examples.en: She treats every creature with care.
examples.cn: 她对每个生灵都很爱护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creature 记成 create（创造）加 -ure：被造出来、还会自己动的东西，就是生物。

root: 源自拉丁语 creare（创造、生长），经 creatura（被造之物）而来；本义是「被造出来的活物」，后专指动物，也可带感情地指人。

sensesIntro.en: From any living thing, to an animal, to a person spoken of with feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任何活物，到动物，再到带着感情去说的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bright eyes in the grass at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里草丛中两点发亮的眼睛。

branches.en: Anything alive and breathing is a creature.
branches.cn: 一切活着会呼吸的都是生物。

branches.en: Small animals are the creatures we meet most often.
branches.cn: 小动物是我们最常遇到的生物。

branches.en: A person can be called a creature when we feel pity.
branches.cn: 心里怜悯时，人可以被称为生物。

branches.en: The same word covers a beetle and a beggar.
branches.cn: 同一个词既盖住甲虫，也盖住乞丐。

branches.en: An unnamed animal is simply a creature in the dark.
branches.cn: 叫不出名的动物，就是黑暗里的一只生物。

intro.en: Creature belongs to the Latin family of creare, to make, which also gives create and creation.
intro.cn: creature 属于拉丁语 creare（制造）这一族，create 与 creation 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root creare, to bring forth, runs through the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 creare（使产生）贯穿这一整族词。

items.example: The creature slept in the leaves.
They create a new game each week.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周造一个新游戏。

items.meaning: the act or result of making

items.exampleCN: 她有一颗善于创造的心。

items.meaning: in the manner of a creature
items.exampleCN: 它带着生物般的谨慎移动。
粗心的手把形状造坏了。

definition_en: trust that allows later payment, praise for something done, or a unit of study
core_image: 店主在小本子上写下你的名字，让你下个月再付钱
scene: 小店的老板没要现金，只在本子上写下他的名字。The shop gave him credit and let him pay next month.
sceneCN: 这里 credit 指「赊账」（第 1 个义项：先拿货后付款的信任）；句意是店家让他赊账，下个月再付钱。

senses.title: Buy now, pay later
senses.definition: an arrangement to take goods now and pay for them later
senses.definitionCN: 先取货、后付款的安排
senses.example: He bought the bicycle on credit.
senses.exampleCN: 他赊账买了那辆自行车。
senses.why: Trust is written in a book and becomes money.
senses.whyCN: 信任被写进本子，就变成了钱。

senses.title: Praise for what was done
senses.definition: praise or approval given to someone for an act
senses.definitionCN: 因某件事给予某人的称赞或认可
senses.example: She deserves credit for the rescue.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援她功不可没。
senses.why: A good act is entered under the name of the doer.
senses.whyCN: 一件好事会被记在做这件事的人名下。

senses.title: A unit of study
senses.definition: a unit that measures work completed in a course
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一门课程完成量的单位
senses.example: The course carries four credits.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课有四个学分。
senses.why: Hours in class are counted and stored like money.
senses.whyCN: 上课的时数被数出来，像钱一样存着。

intro.en: Credit goes back to Latin credere, to believe, and creditum, a thing entrusted.
intro.cn: credit 可追到拉丁语 credere（相信）与 creditum（托付之物）。

items.en: Credere meant to believe a person or a report.
items.cn: credere 意为相信一个人或一则说法。

items.en: Creditum named money or goods entrusted to another.
items.cn: creditum 指托付给他人的钱或货物。

items.en: Credit named trust placed in a person.
items.cn: credit 指对一个人寄予的信任。

items.en: Credit came to mean trust that allows later payment.
items.cn: credit 开始指允许延后付款的信任。

items.en: Banks turned that trust into formal accounts.
items.cn: 银行把这种信任变成了正式账户。

items.en: It also means praise and a unit of study.
items.cn: 它也表示赞扬与一种学业单位。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- stem of believing, and the meaning group names trust and borrowed money.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示相信的 cred- 词干，近义组列出信任与借款的说法。

entries.definition: a short statement of belief
able to be believed
a proof of a person's right or skill
entries.definitionCN: 证明资格或本领的凭据

entries.definition: firm belief in someone
money lent and to be repaid
words that approve of someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a name in a shop book to a line of praise in a report.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从店本子上的一个名字，跑到报告里的一句赞扬。

normal.en: Credit and creed share a root: both rest on belief.

examples.en: A film crew set up its cameras in the square.
examples.cn: 一个摄制组在广场上架起了摄影机。

root: 源自古法语 creue（增援、补充），再往上是拉丁语 crescere（生长、增加）；本义是补充上来的兵员，后指一同干活的一队人，尤其船上与机上的人。

branches.en: An aircraft carries the same team into the sky.
branches.cn: 飞机把同样的一队人带上天空。

branches.en: Any shared job gathers its own small crew.

scene: 玻璃碎了一地，警报在街上响起来。Stealing that car was a serious crime.
sceneCN: 这里 crime 指「罪行」（第 1 个义项：违反法律、应受惩罚的行为）；句意是偷那辆车是一项严重的罪行。

senses.title: An act against the law
senses.definition: an act that breaks the law and can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律、可受惩罚的行为
senses.example: Theft is a crime in every country.
senses.exampleCN: 偷窃在任何国家都是罪行。
senses.why: A rule without a penalty is only advice.

senses.title: Illegal activity as a whole

senses.title: A shameful wrong

senses.why: People borrow the word to weigh moral guilt.
senses.whyCN: 人们借用这个词来衡量道德上的过错。

intro.en: Crime comes from Latin crimen, a charge or accusation, through Old French.
intro.cn: crime 源自拉丁语 crimen（指控、罪名），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Crimen meant a charge or accusation.
items.cn: crimen 意为指控或罪名。

items.en: It also named the fault behind the charge.
items.cn: 它也指指控背后的那桩过错。

items.en: Crime named a wrong that could be judged.
items.cn: crime 指可受审判的过错。

items.en: Crime meant an act that broke the law.
items.cn: crime 指违反法律的行为。

items.en: It also covered illegal activity in general.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crim- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of wrongdoing.

branches.cn: 两个意思都在谴责，一个在法庭，一个在心里。

intro.en: Criminal adds -inal to the Latin stem crim-, the same stem as crime.
intro.cn: criminal 在拉丁词干 crim- 后加 -inal，与 crime 同干。

latinIntro.en: Latin crimen, a charge, gives criminal, criminology and incriminate alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crimen（指控）同时生出 criminal、criminology 与 incriminate。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the law
items.exampleCN: 那名罪犯一言不发地站着。
这笔钱是以犯罪手段取得的。
犯罪学解释盗窃的规律。

items.example: The report measured criminality by district.
items.exampleCN: 报告按区衡量了犯罪状况。
这盘录音使两名男子显得有罪。

items.meaning: a charge made back at an accuser
items.meaningCN: 反过来对指控者的指责

items.meaning: to remove the criminal status of something
items.example: They voted to decriminalize the offence.
items.exampleCN: 他们投票把这一行为除罪化。

definition_en: a time of great danger or difficulty that must be dealt with at once
core_image: 水位不断上涨，堤坝上的人只剩几个小时做决定
scene: 河水快漫过堤顶，所有人都在等一个决定。The flood brought the town to a crisis.
sceneCN: 这里 crisis 指「危机」（第 1 个义项：必须立即应对的危险时刻）；句意是洪水把小镇推到了危机之中。

senses.title: A time of great danger
senses.definition: a moment of great danger when a decision must be made quickly
senses.definitionCN: 必须迅速做出决定的极度危险的时刻
senses.example: The country faced a serious economic crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家面临严重的经济危机。
senses.why: Danger that waits becomes damage that cannot be undone.
senses.whyCN: 拖延的危险，会变成无法挽回的损失。

senses.title: The turning point
senses.definition: the point in an illness or a story where things must turn better or worse
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或事情发展到必须转好或转坏的关头
senses.example: The fever reached its crisis on the third night.
senses.exampleCN: 高烧在第三天夜里到了紧要关头。
senses.why: An illness also arrives at a fork and must choose a side.
senses.whyCN: 疾病也会走到一个岔口，必须选一边。

senses.title: A lasting hard state
senses.definition: a continuing state of serious difficulty in a society or system
senses.definitionCN: 社会或系统中持续存在的严重困难状态
senses.example: The housing crisis has lasted for years.
senses.exampleCN: 住房困境已经持续多年。
senses.why: Some turning points never quite turn, and become everyday life.
senses.whyCN: 有些转折点始终没转过去，就成了日常。

intro.en: Crisis comes from Greek krisis, a decision, from krinein, to separate or judge.
intro.cn: crisis 源自希腊语 krisis（决断），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开或判断。

items.en: Krisis named a decision or a turning point.
items.cn: krisis 指决断或转折点。

items.en: Medical Latin used crisis for the decisive point of an illness.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 crisis 指疾病的决定性时刻。

items.en: Crisis entered English first as a medical term.
items.cn: crisis 最初作为医学术语进入英语。

items.en: It spread to politics, money and daily life.
items.cn: 它扩展到政治、金钱与日常生活。

items.en: It now names any dangerous turning point.
items.cn: 今天它指任何危险的转折点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cri- stem of judging, and the meaning group names other moments of danger.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示判断的 cri- 词干，近义组列出其他危险的时刻。

entries.definition: a person who judges works or actions
very serious, or very important
entries.definitionCN: 非常严重或非常关键的

entries.definition: words that judge faults or merits
a sudden dangerous event needing quick action
entries.definitionCN: 需要迅速行动的突发危险事件

entries.definition: a particular point in time or events
entries.definitionCN: 时间或事件中的某个特定节点

entries.definition: a difficult situation hard to escape

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with rising water and end with a fork that never closes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从上涨的水开始，最后落到一个始终没合上的岔口。

normal.en: Crisis and critic share a root: both are about judging.
normal.cn: crisis 与 critic 同根：两者都关乎判断。

normal.en: A crisis is a clock with no spare hours.
normal.cn: 危机是一只没有多余时辰的钟。

normal.en: Two roads open, and neither waits.
normal.cn: 两条路一起打开，谁也不等你。

normal.en: The word sounds like cry, and someone always cries.
normal.cn: 这个词听着像 cry，而总有人在哭。

normal.en: A long crisis is just a turn that never came.
normal.cn: 漫长的危机，只是一个始终没来的转折。

abstract.en: Picture water an inch below the top of a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象水面离墙顶只差一寸。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone looks at one clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人都盯着同一只钟。

abstract.en: Picture a road split with no sign at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成两岔，却没有路牌。

examples.en: The government acted quickly during the crisis.
examples.cn: 政府在危机期间行动迅速。

examples.en: Two crises hit the company in one year.
examples.cn: 一年之内两场危机击中了这家公司。

examples.en: The illness passed its crisis before dawn.
examples.cn: 病情在天亮前过了危险期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crisis 记成一个必须当场做决定的岔路口：一步走错，后面全变，这就是危机。

root: 源自希腊语 krisis（决断、判断），再往上是 krinein（分开、辨别）；本义是「必须做出决断的那一刻」，由医学上的危险期扩展到政治、经济与生活的转折关头。

sensesIntro.en: From a dangerous moment that demands a decision, to a turning point, to a difficulty that never turns.
sensesIntro.cn: 从必须决断的危险时刻，到转折点，再到始终没转过去的困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water rising to the top of a dike.
core.cn: 核心意象：水涨到堤坝顶端。

branches.en: Danger grows until a decision can no longer wait.
branches.cn: 危险渐长，直到决断再也不能等。

branches.en: An illness or a story reaches a fork and turns.
branches.cn: 疾病或事情走到岔口，然后转向。

branches.en: When the turn never comes, difficulty becomes normal.
branches.cn: 转折没来时，困难就成了常态。

branches.en: Every crisis is a decision point under pressure.
branches.cn: 每一场危机都是压力下的决断点。

branches.en: Some turning points last so long that they turn into daily life.
branches.cn: 有些转折拖得太久，就变成了日常。

intro.en: Crisis belongs to the Greek family of krinein, to judge, which also gives critic and criterion.
intro.cn: crisis 属于希腊语 krinein（判断）这一族，critic 与 criterion 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Greek stem kri- passed into Latin and English as cri-, the stem of judging.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词干 kri- 经拉丁语进入英语，变成表示判断的 cri-。

items.exampleCN: 这场危机考验了每一位领导者。

items.meaningCN: 非常严重或非常关键的
items.exampleCN: 接下来的一小时至关重要。

items.example: The critic praised the new play.
items.exampleCN: 评论家称赞了这部新戏。
这项计划招来尖锐批评。

items.example: They criticize the choice of site.

items.meaning: a careful judgement of a work
in a way that decides the outcome

latinEntries.example: Greek krisis named the moment of decision.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 krisis 指做出决断的时刻。

definition_en: a standard by which something is judged or decided
core_image: 评委桌上摊着一张打分表，一条条标准逐项勾选
scene: 评委把打分表铺在桌上，一行行对照。Cost was not the only criterion for the choice.
sceneCN: 这里 criterion 指「标准」（第 1 个义项：用来评判或决定事物的依据）；句意是成本并不是这次选择的唯一标准。

senses.title: A standard for judging
senses.definition: a standard by which something is judged or decided
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判或决定某事物的标准
senses.example: Safety is our first criterion.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是我们的第一标准。
senses.why: To choose one thing you must first know what counts.
senses.whyCN: 要挑出一样东西，先得知道什么才算数。

senses.title: One test in a set
senses.definition: one of several tests used together to compare choices
senses.definitionCN: 几项测试之一，共同用来比较各种选择
senses.example: The committee listed five criteria for the award.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为这个奖项列了五项评判指标。
senses.why: A single test can be fooled; several together rarely are.
senses.whyCN: 单独一项测试容易被骗，几项一起就很难。

senses.title: A rule for sorting
senses.definition: a rule used to put things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 用来把事物分进各组的规则
senses.example: Size is a useful criterion for sorting the samples.
senses.exampleCN: 大小是给样本分类的一个有用依据。
senses.why: To sort is to decide, and every decision needs a rule.
senses.whyCN: 分类就是做决定，而每个决定都需要一条规则。

intro.en: Criterion comes from Greek kriterion, a means of judging, from krites, a judge.
intro.cn: criterion 源自希腊语 kriterion（判断的手段），再往上是 krites（法官）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate, to decide or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开、决定或判断。

items.en: Krites named a judge or an interpreter.
items.cn: krites 指法官或解释者。

items.en: Kriterion named the tool or test used to judge.
items.cn: kriterion 指用来判断的工具或检验。

items.en: Criterion entered English as a word for a test of truth.
items.cn: criterion 作为检验真伪的词进入英语。

items.en: It spread to science, business and daily choices.
items.cn: 它扩展到科学、商业与日常选择。

items.en: Its Greek plural criteria is now more common than criterions.
items.cn: 它的希腊式复数 criteria 现在比 criterions 更常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crit- stem, and the meaning group names other standards of judgement.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crit- 词干，近义组列出其他用于评判的标准。

entries.definition: a person who judges works
very important or very serious
entries.definitionCN: 非常重要的或非常严重的

entries.definition: the plural form of criterion
a level of quality people expect
a way of judging size or worth
entries.definitionCN: 衡量大小或价值的方式

entries.definition: a known point used for comparison

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a score sheet and end with a rule for sorting boxes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张评分表开始，最后落到分箱子的规则。

normal.en: Criterion and critic share a root: the judge and the ruler.
normal.cn: criterion 与 critic 同根：一个是尺，一个是拿尺的人。

normal.en: A criterion is a ruler you cannot see.
normal.cn: 标准是一把看不见的尺。

normal.en: Five boxes ticked, one choice made.
normal.cn: 五个格子打完勾，一个选择就定了。

normal.en: No criterion means no argument, only taste.
normal.cn: 没有标准，就没有争论，只剩口味。

normal.en: Criteria is one word wearing a Greek plural.
normal.cn: criteria 是一个披着希腊复数的词。

abstract.en: Picture a clean sheet with neat rows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干净的表，横线排得整齐。

abstract.en: Picture a hand hovering over two boxes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在两个格子之间悬着。

abstract.en: Picture two piles sorted by one line.
abstract.cn: 想象两堆东西按同一条线分开。

examples.en: Price is only one criterion for buying a car.
examples.cn: 价格只是买车的一项标准。

examples.en: The plan failed to meet the safety criteria.
examples.cn: 这项计划未能符合安全标准。

examples.en: Kindness was her main criterion for a friend.
examples.cn: 善良是她选朋友的主要标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 criterion 记成评委手里的那把尺：量一量，够不够格，这把尺就是标准。

root: 源自希腊语 kriterion（判断的手段），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）；本义是「用来判定真假好坏的那把尺」，即标准与准则。

sensesIntro.en: From one standard of judgement, to a set of tests, to a rule for sorting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条评判标准，到一组检验指标，再到一条分类规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a score sheet with neat rows of ticks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张横线整齐、逐项打勾的评分表。

branches.en: A standard tells us what counts as good.
branches.cn: 标准告诉我们什么才算好。

branches.en: Several tests together guard against one false signal.
branches.cn: 几项检验合起来，防止一个假信号。

branches.en: A rule of sorting turns a crowd into groups.
branches.cn: 一条分类规则把一堆东西分成几组。

branches.en: Each test borrows its authority from the same standard.
branches.cn: 每项检验的权威都来自同一条标准。

branches.en: Testing and sorting are both acts of separating.
branches.cn: 检验和分类，都是把东西分开的动作。

intro.en: Criterion is a Greek loanword whose stem crit- also builds critic and critical.
intro.cn: criterion 是希腊语借词，它的词干 crit- 也构成 critic 与 critical。

latinIntro.en: The Greek krinein, to judge, reached English through Latin as the stem crit-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 krinein（判断）经拉丁语进入英语，成为词干 crit-。

items.example: The paper sets out criterial rules.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文列出了标准规则。
她那双评判的眼睛什么都没漏掉。

items.meaning: to judge and point out faults
items.example: Do not criticize before you understand.
items.exampleCN: 没弄懂之前别急着批评。
带着判断去读这份报告。

latinEntries.meaning: a means or test of judging
latinEntries.example: Greek kriterion named the judge's tool.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 kriterion 指法官手里的工具。

definition_zh: 批评家；评论家；爱挑剔的人
definition_en: a person who judges and comments on works or on the actions of others
core_image: 一个人坐在台下，边看演出边在节目单上写满批注
scene: 演出还没结束，他就已经在节目单边缘写满批注。The critic left before the final act.
sceneCN: 这里 critic 指「评论家」（第 1 个义项：公开评判艺术作品的人）；句意是那位评论家在最后一幕之前就离场了。

pos.zh: 批评家；评论家；爱挑剔的人

senses.title: A judge of art or writing
senses.definition: a person who judges books, films, music or art in public
senses.definitionCN: 公开评判书籍、电影、音乐或艺术的人
senses.example: The critic praised her first novel.
senses.exampleCN: 那位评论家称赞了她的第一部小说。
senses.why: Someone must tell the public what is worth its time.
senses.whyCN: 总得有人告诉公众，什么值得花时间。

senses.title: A person who finds faults
senses.definition: a person who says what is wrong with something
senses.definitionCN: 指出某事哪里不对的人
senses.example: He is a harsh critic of the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这项新政策的严厉批评者。
senses.why: The same judging eye can be turned on any plan.
senses.whyCN: 同一双评判的眼睛，也能转向任何计划。

intro.en: Critic comes from Greek kritikos, able to judge, from krinein, to judge.
intro.cn: critic 源自希腊语 kritikos（善于判断的），再往上是 krinein（判断）。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate, to decide or to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开、决定或判断。

items.en: Kritikos described a person able to judge.
items.cn: kritikos 形容有能力判断的人。

items.en: Criticus named the judge of a text or a work.
items.cn: criticus 指评判文本或作品的人。

items.en: Critic named a learned judge of literature.
items.cn: critic 指博学的文学评判者。

items.en: It spread to art, music and the theatre.
items.cn: 它扩展到美术、音乐与戏剧。

items.en: It also means anyone who points out faults.
items.cn: 它也指任何指出缺点的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crit- stem, and the meaning group names other people who comment in public.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crit- 词干，近义组列出其他公开发表评论的人。

the act of judging faults
a careful written judgement
a person who writes about new works
a person who explains and judges events

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a pencil in the dark and end with a sharp word at a meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从黑暗里的一支笔开始，最后落到会上的一句尖话。

normal.en: Critic and crisis share a root: a judgement must be made.
normal.cn: critic 与 crisis 同根：总要有人做出判断。

normal.en: The critic watches the play twice and writes once.
normal.cn: 评论家看两遍戏，只写一遍字。

normal.en: Every margin is full of small marks.
normal.cn: 每一处页边都写满小记号。

normal.en: A good critic names the fault and the reason.
normal.cn: 好的批评者既指出毛病，也说出理由。

normal.en: Anyone can criticize; a critic is paid to be fair.
normal.cn: 谁都会批评，而评论家是靠公道吃饭的。

abstract.en: Picture a seat at the back of a dark theatre.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中剧院后排的一个座位。

abstract.en: Picture a page crowded with tiny notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一页挤满小字的批注。

abstract.en: Picture a raised eyebrow at a long meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象长会上一个挑起的眉毛。

examples.en: The critic called the film a masterpiece.
examples.cn: 这位评论家称这部电影是杰作。

examples.en: Critics of the plan want more evidence.
examples.cn: 这项计划的批评者想要更多证据。

examples.en: She became a food critic after ten years of cooking.
examples.cn: 做了十年菜之后，她成了美食评论家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 critic 记成拿着小本子坐在台下的那个人：看完就写，写的就是评判。

root: 源自希腊语 kritikos（善于判断的），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）；本义是「有能力评判的人」，后专指公开评论作品的人，也指爱挑毛病的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the public judge of art to anyone who names a fault.
sensesIntro.cn: 从公开评判艺术的人，到任何指出毛病的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil moving in the dark of a theatre.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗剧院里移动的一支铅笔。

branches.en: The critic turns a private evening into public opinion.
branches.cn: 评论家把一个私人夜晚变成公众意见。

branches.en: The same eye can be turned on a policy or a person.
branches.cn: 同一双眼睛也能转向一项政策或一个人。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the act of judging.
branches.cn: 两个义项都立在评判这一动作上。

branches.en: A review needs both knowledge and fairness.
branches.cn: 一篇评论既需要知识，也需要公道。

branches.en: A critic who never praises soon loses readers.
branches.cn: 从不称赞的批评者，很快会失去读者。

intro.en: Critic is the short stem word behind critical, criticism and critique.
intro.cn: critic 是那个短词干，critical、criticism 与 critique 都由它长出。

latinIntro.en: Greek krinein, to judge, became the Latin and English stem crit-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 krinein（判断）变成了拉丁语与英语里的词干 crit-。

items.example: The critic wrote three lines only.
items.exampleCN: 那位评论家只写了三行。

items.example: She gave the plan a critical look.
items.exampleCN: 她用评判的眼光看了看计划。

items.example: His criticism was short and fair.

items.meaning: a written judgement of a work
items.example: He wrote a critique of the design.
items.exampleCN: 他写了对这个设计的评论。
她带着判断读了这封信。
这位评论家说出了自己的标准。

latinEntries.example: Greek kritikos described a skilled judge.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 kritikos 形容善于判断的人。

definition_zh: 关键的；危急的；批判的；挑剔的
definition_en: extremely important, very serious, or ready to judge faults
core_image: 医生站在病床前，盯着监护仪上跳动的数字
scene: 医生盯着监护仪，数字忽然往下掉。The next few hours will be critical for the patient.
sceneCN: 这里 critical 指「危急的」（第 1 个义项：生死攸关、极其严重的）；句意是接下来几个小时对病人来说十分危急。

pos.zh: 关键的；危急的；批判的；挑剔的

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.definition: so important that the whole outcome depends on it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到整个结果都取决于它
senses.example: Timing is critical in this experiment.

senses.exampleCN: 他在大学教文学批评。

examples.en: Farmers here grow three crops a year.
examples.cn: 这里的农民一年种三季作物。

examples.en: The corn crop survived the dry summer.
examples.cn: 玉米收成熬过了干旱的夏天。

examples.en: A new crop of problems cropped up at once.
examples.cn: 一批新问题一下子冒了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crop 记成从植物顶端割下来的那一把：一季的庄稼，就是收成。

root: 源自古英语 cropp（植物顶端、穗），后指从田里收上来的谷物，再引申为一季的收成、同时出现的一批，以及剪短的动作。

sensesIntro.en: From what grows in the field, to what the field gives, to a group that arrives together.
sensesIntro.cn: 从田里种的东西，到田里给出的收成，再到一起到来的一批。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field of wheat turning gold in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：风里翻成金色的麦田。

branches.en: The planted plants are the crop itself.
branches.cn: 种下去的植物本身就是作物。

branches.en: The gathered amount is the season's crop.
branches.cn: 收回来的数量，就是这一季的收成。

branches.en: A group arriving together borrows the field image.
branches.cn: 同时到来的一批，借用了田里的意象。

branches.en: What is planted and what is gathered share one word.
branches.cn: 种下的和收回的，共用一个词。

branches.en: Both a harvest and a class are counted as one lot.
branches.cn: 收成和一个班，都被算作一整批。

intro.en: Crop is a short Old English word that builds compounds like cropland and sharecropper.
intro.cn: crop 是古英语的短词，能组成 cropland、sharecropper 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin base is involved; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基，它是英语本族词。

items.example: The crop stood tall in June.

items.exampleCN: 这些田里种着两季作物。

items.meaning: the act of growing or cutting
a farmer who pays rent in crops
items.exampleCN: 这位分成制农民留下三分之一。

items.meaning: a season with almost no harvest

definition_zh: 十字形；叉号；穿过；生气的
definition_en: to go from one side to the other, or a mark made by two lines
core_image: 两条大路在地图正中交成一个十字
scene: 地图上两条大路在城中心交成一个十字。We had to cross the river before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 cross 指「穿过」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边）；句意是我们必须在天黑前过河。

senses.title: Go from one side to the other
senses.definition: to go from one side of something to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从某物的一边走到另一边
senses.example: She crossed the bridge slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢地过了桥。
senses.why: The shortest way between two banks is a line straight over.
senses.whyCN: 两岸之间最短的路，就是一条直着过去的线。

senses.title: A mark of two lines
senses.definition: a shape or mark made when one line passes over another
senses.definitionCN: 一条线压过另一条线所形成的形状或记号
senses.example: Put a cross beside the wrong answer.
senses.exampleCN: 在错误答案旁边画一个叉。
senses.why: Two paths meet at a point, and the point can be written down.
senses.whyCN: 两条路交于一点，而这一点可以被写下来。

senses.title: Annoyed
senses.definition: annoyed or angry, used in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 恼火或生气，多用于日常口语
senses.example: He was cross with me for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为我迟到而生气。
senses.why: A mood can cut across a face like a line drawn sharply.
senses.whyCN: 情绪能像一条硬线一样横切过一张脸。

intro.en: Cross comes from Latin crux, a cross, through Old Irish and Old Norse forms.
intro.cn: cross 源自拉丁语 crux（十字架），经古爱尔兰语与古诺斯语形式进入英语。

items.en: Crux named a cross or a gallows.
items.cn: crux 指十字架或刑架。

items.en: Cruciare meant to put someone on a cross.
items.cn: cruciare 意为把人钉上十字架。

items.en: Cros named the shape carried by monks.
items.cn: cros 指修士所带的十字形。

items.en: Kross kept the same shape and name.
items.cn: kross 保留了同样的形状与名称。

items.en: Cross entered English as the name of the shape.
items.cn: cross 作为形状的名称进入英语。

items.en: The verb means to pass over, and the adjective means annoyed.
items.cn: 动词意为越过，形容词意为恼火。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cross spelling, and the meaning group names other ways of going over or meeting.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cross 这串拼写，近义组列出其他越过与相交的说法。

entries.definition: from one side to the other
a place or act of going over
a place where two roads meet
to travel across a whole area
to cut through or meet at a point
to stretch from one side to the other

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two roads meeting and end with a short sharp mood.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两条路相交开始，最后落到一点就着的脾气。

normal.en: Two lines make a cross, and a cross is a doorway.
normal.cn: 两条线画成一个十字，而十字就是一扇门。

normal.en: To cross is to leave one bank and arrive at the other.
normal.cn: 穿过，就是离开这一岸，到达那一岸。

normal.en: A cross on paper means no; a cross on water means through.
normal.cn: 纸上的叉表示不行，水面上的叉表示过去。

normal.en: A cross face is a line drawn hard across the brow.
normal.cn: 生气的脸，是眉间被狠狠画了一道线。

normal.en: One word carries a shape, a journey and a mood.
normal.cn: 一个词，带着一个形状、一段路和一种情绪。

abstract.en: Picture two roads cutting a square in half.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路把一个方块从中切开。

abstract.en: Picture a boat moving toward the far bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船驶向对岸。

abstract.en: Picture a pen striking out a wrong word.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔把一个错字划掉。

examples.en: Look both ways before you cross.
examples.cn: 过马路前先看两边。

examples.en: A red cross marks the hospital on the map.
examples.cn: 地图上一个红十字标出医院。

examples.en: She was cross with herself for forgetting.
examples.cn: 她因为忘记而生自己的气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cross 记成两条路交出的十字：从十字的一边走到另一边，就是穿过。

root: 源自拉丁语 crux（十字架、刑架），经古爱尔兰语与古诺斯语进入英语；由十字的形状生出交叉、穿过的动作，再由绷紧的脸引申为生气。

sensesIntro.en: From a shape of two lines, to the act of passing over, to the mood drawn on a face.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两条线构成的形状，到越过去的动作，再到脸上画出的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two roads meeting at one point on a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上两条路交于一点。

branches.en: The crossing itself is a movement from side to side.
branches.cn: 穿过本身就是从一边到另一边的移动。

branches.en: The written cross freezes that meeting point.
branches.cn: 写下的十字，把这个交点固定住。

branches.en: A sharp mood cuts across the face like a line.
branches.cn: 尖锐的情绪像一条线横切过脸。

branches.en: A crossroads is a written cross made walkable.
branches.cn: 十字路口，就是一个能走上去的十字。

branches.en: Both a mark and a mood can be short and sharp.
branches.cn: 记号和情绪，都可以又短又利。

intro.en: Cross is a short word that joins with many others to name places and actions.
intro.cn: cross 是个短词，能与许多词结合，命名地点与动作。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crux, a cross, is the distant source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux（十字）是这一整族词的远源。

items.meaning: to go over, or a cross shape
items.exampleCN: 他们在红绿灯处过了马路。

items.meaning: a place or act of going over
items.example: Use the crossing near the school.
items.exampleCN: 走学校附近的那条人行横道。

items.meaning: goes over, or more than one cross
items.example: The ferry crosses twice a day.
The shop stands at the crossroads.

items.exampleCN: 他生气地答了一句就走了。

items.meaning: from one side to the other
items.example: The bank is across the street.

items.meaning: a word puzzle of crossing lines
items.example: She solves a crossword each morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上做一道填字游戏。

latinEntries.example: Latin crux named the wooden cross.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 crux 指木制的十字架。

definition_en: a large number of people gathered close together, or to fill a place
core_image: 广场上人挤人，连转身的地方都没有
scene: 广场上人挤人，连转身都困难。A crowd had gathered outside the station.
sceneCN: 这里 crowd 指「人群」（第 1 个义项：密集聚在一起的一大群人）；句意是车站外已经聚起了一群人。

senses.title: Many people in one place
senses.definition: a large number of people gathered close together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 密集聚集在同一地点的一大群人
senses.example: The crowd cheered as the team scored.
senses.exampleCN: 球队得分时人群欢呼起来。
senses.why: Many bodies in a small space become one moving thing.
senses.whyCN: 许多身体挤在狭小空间里，就变成一具会移动的东西。

senses.title: Ordinary people as a whole
senses.definition: the mass of ordinary people, not leaders or experts
senses.definitionCN: 普通人的整体，而非领袖或专家
senses.example: The song was first sung by the crowd, not the choir.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌先由群众唱起来，而不是唱诗班。
senses.why: A mass of people can be spoken of as a single force.
senses.whyCN: 一大群人，可以被当成一股力量来说。

senses.title: Fill a place tightly
senses.definition: to fill a space so that there is little room left
senses.definitionCN: 把空间填满，几乎不留余地
senses.example: Fans crowded the entrance before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天没亮粉丝就挤满了入口。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb when the mass starts to press in.
senses.whyCN: 当人群开始往里压，名词就变成了动词。

intro.en: Crowd comes from Old English crudan, to press or push.
intro.cn: crowd 源自古英语 crudan，意为挤压、推。

items.en: Crudan meant to press or push.
items.cn: crudan 意为挤压或推。

items.en: Croude named a pushing throng of people.
items.cn: croude 指互相推挤的一群人。

items.en: Crowd named a large company of people.
items.cn: crowd 指一大群人。

items.en: The verb meant to press into a place.
items.cn: 动词形式意为挤进一个地方。

items.en: It spread to any tightly packed group.
items.cn: 它扩展到任何紧密挤在一起的一群。

items.en: It also means ordinary people as a whole.
items.cn: 它也指整体意义上的普通群众。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crowd spelling, and the meaning group names other large groups of people.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crowd 这串拼写，近义组列出其他大群人的说法。

entries.definition: full of too many people
the act of pressing into a space
holding far too many people
a dense crowd pressing together
a crowd that may become violent
people gathered to watch or listen
entries.definitionCN: 聚起来观看或倾听的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with bodies pressed together and end with a voice called the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从挤在一起的身体开始，最后落到被称为人民的那个声音。

normal.en: Crowd comes from pushing: many shoulders in one doorway.
normal.cn: crowd 来自推挤：一道门口挤着许多肩膀。

normal.en: One face is a person; a thousand faces are a crowd.
normal.cn: 一张脸是一个人，一千张脸就是人群。

normal.en: A crowd has no single mind, yet it moves as one.
normal.cn: 人群没有统一的头脑，却能像一个整体那样移动。

normal.en: When people press in, the noun becomes a verb.
normal.cn: 人往里一挤，名词就变成了动词。

normal.en: Stand out from the crowd by standing still.
normal.cn: 想从人群里显出来，就站住不动。

abstract.en: Picture a square filled shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象广场上肩挨着肩。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred hands raised at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一百只手同时举起。

abstract.en: Picture one voice coming out of many mouths.
abstract.cn: 想象许多张嘴里传出同一个声音。

examples.en: A crowd gathered to watch the street singer.
examples.cn: 一群人聚起来看街头歌手。

examples.en: The crowd pushed toward the open gate.
examples.cn: 人群朝敞开的大门挤去。

examples.en: Tourists crowd the old town every summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天游客挤满这座老城。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crowd 记成一道门口挤满的肩膀：人一多、一挤，就成了人群。

root: 源自古英语 crudan（挤压、推）；本义是「互相推挤的一群人」，由挤压的动作生出人群之义，再作动词表示挤满、聚集。

sensesIntro.en: From bodies packed in one place, to the people as a whole, to the act of pressing in.
sensesIntro.cn: 从挤在一处的身体，到作为整体的群众，再到往里挤的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoulders packed tight in a square.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上紧紧相挨的肩膀。

branches.en: A tight mass of people becomes a single presence.
branches.cn: 密集的一群人，变成一个有存在感的东西。

branches.en: The same mass can stand for ordinary people.
branches.cn: 同一群人，也能代表普通民众。

branches.en: When the mass presses in, the word turns into a verb.
branches.cn: 当这群人往里压，这个词就变成动词。

branches.en: A crowd can be counted and also spoken of as one force.
branches.cn: 人群既能被计数，也能被当成一股力量。

branches.en: People in the street both are the crowd and crowd the street.
branches.cn: 街上的人既是人群，也在挤满街道。

intro.en: Crowd is a native English word that builds crowded, crowding and overcrowded.
intro.cn: crowd 是英语本族词，能组成 crowded、crowding 与 overcrowded。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word grew from the old verb for pressing.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词基，它从表示挤压的古动词长出来。

items.example: The crowding at the gate was dangerous.
The square stood crowdless at dawn.

items.meaning: keeping a large group safe and orderly

definition_en: a circle worn on the head by a ruler, or the top part of something
core_image: 一顶镶着宝石的金冠稳稳压在王座上方那颗头上
scene: 加冕那天，金冠被缓缓放到新王头上。The crown passed to his daughter.
sceneCN: 这里 crown 指「王冠」（第 1 个义项：君主戴在头上的环形饰物）；句意是王冠传给了他的女儿。

senses.title: A ruler's circle of gold
senses.definition: a circle of gold and jewels worn on the head by a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 君主戴在头上的金玉环形饰物
senses.example: The crown sat on a velvet cushion.
senses.exampleCN: 王冠放在一只天鹅绒垫子上。
senses.why: A circle on the head marks the one who stands above all.
senses.whyCN: 头顶一个圆环，标出那个高过所有人的人。

senses.title: Royal power itself
senses.definition: the power or position of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王所拥有的权力或地位
senses.example: He gave up the crown for love.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了爱放弃了王位。
senses.why: The object stands for the office it marks.
senses.whyCN: 那件实物，代表了它所标记的那个位置。

senses.title: The highest part
senses.definition: the top or highest part of a head, a tree or a hill
senses.definitionCN: 头、树或山最高的那部分
senses.example: A bird sat on the crown of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸟停在树顶。
senses.why: The top of anything wears a small crown of its own.
senses.whyCN: 任何东西的顶部，都自带一顶小冠。

intro.en: Crown comes from Latin corona, a wreath, through Old French corone.
intro.cn: crown 源自拉丁语 corona（花环），经古法语 corone 进入英语。

items.en: Corona meant a wreath or a circle.
items.cn: corona 指花环或圆环。

items.en: It was given to victors and to brides.
items.cn: 它被戴在胜利者与新娘头上。

items.en: Corone named a royal circlet.
items.cn: corone 指君王所戴的环形冠。

items.en: Crown named the king's circlet.
items.cn: crown 指国王的环形冠冕。

items.en: It came to mean royal power itself.
items.cn: 它开始指王权本身。

items.en: It also names the top of a head, a hill or a tooth.
items.cn: 它也指头、山或牙齿的顶部。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crown spelling, and the meaning group names other seats or signs of royal power.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crown 这串拼写，近义组列出其他王权的象征与位置。

entries.definition: having a crown, or made king
entries.definitionCN: 戴着王冠的，或被立为王的

entries.definition: forming the finest final point
without a crown or a ruler
the seat and office of a ruler
a small crown worn by a noble
a ring of leaves or flowers

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a ring of gold and end with the top of an old tree.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个金环开始，最后落到一棵老树的顶梢。

normal.en: Crown began as a wreath, and a wreath is a circle.
normal.cn: crown 本是花环，而花环就是一个圆。

normal.en: A circle has no beginning, which suits a king.
normal.cn: 圆没有起点，这正合一位君王。

normal.en: The crown is heavy because the office is.
normal.cn: 冠很重，因为那个位置很重。

normal.en: Every hill wears its own crown of trees.
normal.cn: 每一座山都戴着属于自己的树冠。

normal.en: To crown a day is to give it a perfect end.
normal.cn: 为一天加冕，就是给它一个完美的结尾。

abstract.en: Picture gold resting on red velvet.
abstract.cn: 想象金子搁在红色天鹅绒上。

abstract.en: Picture a head bowed to receive a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗低下去接住圆环的头。

abstract.en: Picture a single tree above the whole forest.
abstract.cn: 想象整片林子之上的一棵树。

examples.en: The crown was kept in a locked room.
examples.cn: 王冠被锁在一间屋子里。

examples.en: She succeeded to the crown at twenty.
examples.cn: 她二十岁继承王位。

examples.en: Snow crowned the top of the mountain.
examples.cn: 雪覆盖了山顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 crown 记成头顶上那个金环：戴上它是王冠，戴在山上就是山顶。

root: 源自拉丁语 corona（花环、圆环），经古法语 corone 进入英语；本义是戴在头上的环，后指王冠与王权，再引申为任何事物的顶部。

sensesIntro.en: From a circle on a head, to the power it stands for, to the top of anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 从头上的一只圆环，到它所代表的权力，再到任何事物的顶端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold ring resting on a bowed head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只金环落在低下的头顶。

branches.en: The ring itself is the first meaning.
branches.cn: 那只圆环本身，是最早的意思。

branches.en: The object then stands for the power behind it.
branches.cn: 这件实物随后代表了它背后的权力。

branches.en: Any highest point is crowned by its own top.
branches.cn: 任何最高处，都被自己的顶端加冕。

branches.en: Gold and authority are worn together.
branches.cn: 金子和权威，被一起戴在头上。

branches.en: A king and a hill both carry a crown.
branches.cn: 国王和山丘，都顶着一顶冠。

intro.en: Crown is a short word that builds crowned, crowning and uncrowned.
intro.cn: crown 是个短词，能组成 crowned、crowning 与 uncrowned。

latinIntro.en: The Latin corona, a wreath, is the source of crown and of coronation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 corona（花环）是 crown 与 coronation 的源头。

items.meaning: a ring worn by a ruler
items.example: The crown shone under the lamp.
Two crowns were kept in the vault.
The king was crowned at dawn.

items.exampleCN: 最辉煌的一刻出现在最后。

items.example: The crownless prince left the hall.
items.exampleCN: 未戴冠的王子离开了大厅。

items.example: The coronation drew a huge crowd.

items.meaning: a small crown of a noble
items.example: A thin coronet held her hair.
items.exampleCN: 一顶细小的冠束住她的头发。

latinEntries.example: Latin corona first named a wreath.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 corona 最初指花环。
